    Angels¶

    "They are not divine. They only look that way." — Kramsadar dragon, when asked about the beings at the south pole

    Angels are not divine messengers — whatever they may believe about themselves, they are a species that looks angelic: winged, luminous, serene. The name stuck because no one who has seen one has ever come up with anything better.

    An angel is an energy being capable of taking physical form. Their natural state is not flesh, but light — coherent, intelligent patterns of energy that can condense into a humanoid shape when they choose. Most people on Ge'or do not know they are energy beings — angels usually take the form of humans. The winged, luminous form of legend is a choice too, and it is kept for the rare encounters that become stories.

    Nature¶

    • Energy beings — not flesh and blood in the conventional sense. Their bodies are solidified light, sustained by an internal energy core.
    • Light-speed travel — in their energetic form, angels can travel to places at the speed of light.
    • Form-shifting — an angel can take the form of most beings on Ge'or and speak with them. In daily life they usually take the form of humans — most people never realize what they are
    • Whimsical — angels are whimsical creatures by nature and aesthetic.
    • Rare communicators — angels can communicate, but it is super rare; when they do, it is for exceptional cases.
    • Disappearing — when they are seen, usually after a while — or as you get closer — they disappear right in front of you. They tolerate observers up to a point, as long as you do not come too close.
    • Active helpers — although their homeland is the south pole, they are around Ge'or: helping animals, planting trees, fixing broken things, often unseen.
    • Legendary — Ge'or citizens see them as legendary beings that are there to help Ge'or. Sightings are usually of their back, when the angel does not notice the observer's presence. A child may see an angel and smile at him, just for the angel to disappear five seconds later.
    • Not evil — 99.99% of angels are not evil; they strive to make Ge'or a better place.

    Religion¶

    Angels follow Pragmus — they believe themselves to be the creation and employees of the god of Ge'or, and that they should strive to perfect the world.

    Biology¶

    • Appearance: Tall (1.8–2.1 meters), slender, with large feathered wings (spanning 3–4 meters). Pale skin, hair in shades of white, silver, and pale gold. Eyes are luminous — pale blue, silver, or violet
    • Lifespan: 300–500 years. Angels age slowly and are among the longest-lived species on Ge'or
    • Mage-cell expression: The highest baseline of any species. Every angel is born with significant magical ability — light manipulation, flight enhancement, and healing are universal. Combat magic is rarer but devastating
    • Wings: Fully functional. Angels can fly for hours without fatigue. Their feathers are individually prehensile — an angel's wing can gesture with the precision of a hand
    • Cold Adaptation: Perfectly adapted to the polar climate. Angels do not feel cold. Their body temperature runs high, and they can sleep in snow without harm

    Society¶

    Angelic society in Alborric is ancient and insular — the polar mountains have been their home for millennia — yet their presence is felt across Ge'or.

    • Governance: The Luminous Council — seven eldest angels chosen for wisdom, not lineage. Decisions are made by consensus after deliberation that can last years
    • Culture: Austere and contemplative at home; whimsical and light-footed abroad. Angels value silence, study, and the perfection of a single craft over a lifetime
    • Relations: The Dragons of Kramsadar are the only people who regularly interact with them — described as "mutual respect between two peoples who understand what it means to be alone." Most of Ge'or holds angels as legend

    Connections¶

    • Nation: Alborric (Polar Continent)
    • Faith: Pragmus
    • Phenomenon: Angel Apparitions
    • Traits: Winged, long-lived, highest mage-cell expression, light-speed travel, form-shifting, polar-adapted, whimsical helpers
